guide.title: Differential equations: review guide
guide.intro: A differential equation relates a function to its derivative. In AP Calculus AB you write them from descriptions, read slope fields, and solve separable equations, including exponential models.

sections.title: Writing and verifying differential equations
body: “The rate of change of y is proportional to y” means dy/dt = ky. To check that a function is a solution, substitute it and its derivative into the equation.
points: A general solution contains a constant C. An initial condition picks one particular solution.

sections.title: Slope fields
body: A slope field draws a short segment at each point (x, y) with slope dy/dx given by the equation. Solution curves follow the segments.
points: If dy/dx depends only on x, segments in each vertical column are parallel.
If dy/dx depends only on y, segments along each horizontal row are parallel.
Where dy/dx = 0 the segments are horizontal.

sections.title: Separable equations and exponential models
body: Separate the variables (all y with dy, all x with dx), integrate both sides, include + C, then use the initial condition to find C. Solve for y if you can.
points: dy/dt = ky has solution y = y₀e^(kt): growth if k > 0, decay if k < 0.
Add + C right after integrating. Exponentiating turns it into a factor, not an added constant.
Euler's method and logistic models are AP Calculus BC topics, so they are not reviewed here.

example.solution: Separate: dy/y = 2x dx. Integrate: ln|y| = x² + C. So y = Ae^(x²), and y(0) = 5 gives A = 5. The solution is y = 5e^(x²).

misconceptions: Add it when you integrate. After exponentiating it becomes a multiplying factor.
It shows slopes. You still pick one curve using the initial condition.

questions.prompt: Which equation says that the rate of change of P with respect to t is proportional to P?
questions.explanation: “Proportional to P” means the rate equals a constant times P: dP/dt = kP.
choiceExplanations: dP/dt = kt makes the rate proportional to t, not to P.
dP/dt = k is a constant rate, which is not proportional to P.
P = kt describes P itself, not its rate of change.

questions.prompt: Which function is a solution of dy/dx = 2y?
choiceExplanations: For y = 2x + 5, dy/dx = 2, which is not 2(2x + 5).
For y = e^(x²), dy/dx = 2x · e^(x²) = 2xy, not 2y.
For y = x² + 2, dy/dx = 2x, which is not 2(x² + 2).

questions.prompt: In the slope field for dy/dx = x − y, what is the slope of the segment at the point (2, 1)?
choiceExplanations: −1 computes y − x instead of x − y.
2 uses only x and ignores the − y term.
3 adds the coordinates instead of subtracting.
questions.licenseOrRights: Original question written for StudySprint. The linked College Board page was only used to confirm the unit's title and scope.

questions.prompt: What is the solution of dy/dx = xy with y(0) = 3?
questions.explanation: Separate: dy/y = x dx. Integrate: ln|y| = x²/2 + C, so y = Ae^(x²/2). y(0) = 3 gives A = 3.
choiceExplanations: + C was added after exponentiating. e^(x²/2 + C) = A · e^(x²/2), a multiple, not a sum.
This integrates only the x side and forgets that the y side gives ln|y|.
The antiderivative of x is x²/2, not x².
questions.licenseOrRights: Original question written for StudySprint. The linked College Board page was only used to confirm the unit's title and scope.

questions.prompt: In a slope field, every segment along any horizontal line has the same slope, and the segments are horizontal along the line y = 1. Which could be the differential equation?
questions.explanation: Equal slopes along each horizontal line means dy/dx depends only on y. dy/dx = y − 1 does, and it is 0 when y = 1.
choiceExplanations: 1 − x depends only on x, so slopes vary along each horizontal line.
x(y − 1) changes with x along a horizontal line (except where y = 1).
dy/dx = x − 1 depends only on x, so equal slopes appear along vertical lines instead.

questions.prompt: A substance decays exponentially with a half-life of 4 hours. There are 80 g at t = 0. How much remains after 12 hours?
choiceExplanations: 40 g is after one half-life (4 hours).
26.7 g divides 80 by 3. Each half-life halves the amount; it does not subtract a fixed share.
20 g is after two half-lives (8 hours).

questions.prompt: What is the solution of dy/dx = y² with y(0) = 1?
questions.explanation: Separate: y⁻² dy = dx. Integrate: −1/y = x + C. y(0) = 1 gives C = −1, so −1/y = x − 1 and y = 1/(1 − x).
choiceExplanations: This gives y(0) = −1, which does not match the initial condition y(0) = 1.
y = eˣ solves dy/dx = y, not dy/dx = y².
This drops the minus sign: the antiderivative of y⁻² is −1/y.

questions.prompt: Coffee at 90°C sits in a 20°C room, and its temperature satisfies dT/dt = −0.1(T − 20). Which expression gives T(t)?
questions.explanation: Let D = T − 20. Then dD/dt = −0.1D, so D = D₀e^(−0.1t) with D₀ = 90 − 20 = 70. So T = 20 + 70e^(−0.1t), which starts at 90 and approaches 20.
choiceExplanations: This swaps the numbers. It would approach 70°C instead of the room temperature.
This uses 90 as the starting difference. The starting difference is 90 − 20 = 70, so T(0) would be 110.
This ignores the room temperature. It would cool toward 0°C, not 20°C.
